coverage.basis: Initial review covers the preceding month; subsequent reviews should begin after this coverage-through date and deduplicate by normalized DOI/title.

deduplication.title_normalization: lowercase, Unicode normalized, punctuation and repeated whitespace collapsed

topics: estuarine dissolved oxygen dynamics and monitoring
search_protocol.inclusion: Original peer-reviewed paper or authoritative research report newly published or newly available in the coverage window, with a primary source and enough methods detail to assess Mobile Bay transferability.
search_protocol.exclusion: News-only summaries, reviews without new directly useful results, sources outside the window, unverified dates/DOIs, and weakly related work.
search_protocol.verification: Each included record was checked twice: primary article/full text or PDF plus a second bibliographic or publisher-index read.

publications.title: Physicochemical and urban land-use characteristics associated with resistance to precipitation in estuaries vary across scales
institutions: Guana Tolomato Matanzas National Estuarine Research Reserve / Florida Department of Environmental Protection
University of Wisconsin–Madison Division of Extension / Lake Superior National Estuarine Research Reserve
San Francisco State University Estuary and Ocean Science Center

observational_coverage.variables: DO, temperature, turbidity, salinity, depth and meteorology; nutrients and chlorophyll-a from monthly grab samples
observational_coverage.event_design: One relatively wet and one relatively dry year per estuary selected from 1990–2020 precipitation context; major events chosen from named storms and station precipitation subject to data completeness.

publications.methods: Calculated an event resistance index from pre/post dissolved-oxygen change, then related resistance to physicochemical conditions and land-use/population metrics at continental, salinity-group and local-estuary scales. Event-level sensor covariates were paired with event-specific resistance; monthly nutrient/chlorophyll data were averaged annually because sampling did not align with storms.
findings: Urbanized estuaries tended to show greater resistance of dissolved oxygen to precipitation events than less urbanized estuaries, contrary to the authors' initial hypothesis, but the relationship varied among systems.
Water-column depth, temperature, turbidity and chlorophyll-a showed the most recurring associations across scales.

Relationships involving nitrogen, land use, salinity and nutrient ratios changed by salinity class and individual estuary; the study explicitly warns against assuming one storm-response mechanism or sign across estuaries.
Weeks Bay was one of the five systems, making the result geographically relevant while still not measuring Point Clear bottom oxygen or Jubilee biology.
uncertainty_and_limitations: No held-out predictive evaluation or external forecast validation.
Wet/dry years and major events were selected using system-specific criteria and data completeness.
Monthly nutrients and chlorophyll-a were not event-matched and used annual means.
A DO resistance index is not a Jubilee-event label, fish aggregation endpoint or direct hypoxia forecast.
mobile_bay_implications: Do not encode rainfall/runoff as a universally monotonic oxygen-loading feature. Test interactions with salinity, temperature, depth/turbidity, chlorophyll and lags.
Use Weeks Bay as a regional comparator only; retain zero weight until Eastern Shore bottom-state and event/control validation exists.
Offline test whether storm-response features improve event-blocked calibration after direct local oxygen and defensible controls become available.
research_questions: Does predawn Eastern Shore bottom oxygen respond to comparable rain events with the same sign as Weeks Bay, after conditioning on salinity and mixing state?
Which lag and accumulated-rain windows retain incremental value after temperature, salinity, river forcing and observation effort are controlled?
Can event-specific storm windows be constructed without post-event leakage and with enough matched Jubilee/non-event episodes?

publications.title: Tampa Bay observing network: a continuous data acquisition system in support of science and environmental management
institutions: University of South Florida College of Marine Science (lead)
Tampa Bay Estuary Program and regional partners

observational_coverage.water_quality_variables: temperature, conductivity/salinity, pressure/depth, dissolved oxygen, pH, turbidity and chlorophyll-a; FDOM added beginning in 2024
observational_coverage.transport: bottom-mounted Nortek Signature 1000 ADCP at applicable stations; current velocity is non-real-time
observational_coverage.quality_control: automated QARTOD-style gross-range, spike/outlier and rate-of-change tests with flags

publications.methods: Describes technical design, station/instrument architecture, telemetry, data portal and QA/QC, with practical case studies showing how high-frequency observations supplement monthly sampling, fill gaps and retain coverage during acute disturbances.
findings: Monthly sampling cannot resolve rapid physical and biogeochemical variability in a shallow estuary; 15-minute water-quality observations materially improve temporal coverage.
Co-located salinity, oxygen, chlorophyll, meteorology and currents support process interpretation during acute disturbances.
The network demonstrates an operational architecture and data-access model, not a validated hypoxia or fish-event forecasting model.
uncertainty_and_limitations: No out-of-sample forecast comparison, sensitivity/specificity or decision-utility evaluation.
Water-quality sensors are near surface rather than bottom/contact-strip; this cannot substitute for Point Clear bottom oxygen.
ADCP currents are non-real-time and station coverage/operational periods vary.
Case studies are demonstrations selected by the authors, not an independent network benchmark.
mobile_bay_implications: Reinforces the priority of co-timed oxygen, salinity, temperature, chlorophyll/organic-matter proxies, meteorology and current observations with explicit depth and QC.
Supports keeping surface/regional oxygen separate from bottom/contact-strip oxygen and model guidance separate from observed transport.
Offline design opportunity: audit whether existing sources can form 15-minute aligned feature windows with QARTOD-like flags before fitting any event model; no new sensor purchase is implied.
research_questions: Which existing Mobile Bay feeds can be synchronized at 15-minute resolution without conflating surface, mid-depth and bottom measurements?
Do co-located current and oxygen changes precede independently confirmed fish aggregation with useful lead time?
How much forecast value is lost when currents are delayed or model-only rather than real-time observed?

publications.title: Biological legacy of large-scale coastal reclamation: Potential oxygen demand from pre-existing benthic biomass
institutions: Korea Institute of Ocean Science and Technology, East Sea Environment Research Center
University of Science and Technology, School of Ocean Science

observational_coverage.intervention: Final coastal-dike closure in 2006 transformed macrotidal flats and shallow-subtidal habitat into a semi-enclosed system
observational_coverage.data_basis: Field-collected intertidal macrofauna/elevation plus historical biological, hydrological and bathymetric observations; reanalysis of pre/post-closure field observations and prior laboratory retention trajectories
observational_coverage.uncertainty: Conditional parametric bootstrap intervals propagated from biomass and dissolved-oxygen resampling

publications.methods: Reconstructed pre-closure benthic carbon inventory, converted complete decomposition to an oxygen-demand upper bound, constrained affected fractions using observed biomass loss, and compared potential demand with standing oxygen inventories across three assumed effective receiving-water volumes.
findings: Complete decomposition of reconstructed benthic stocks corresponded to an upper-bound potential demand of 25,023 t O2; excluding tidal-flat bacteria reduced it to 14,461 t O2.
At 120 days, two field-constrained biomass-loss estimators produced 3,547 t O2 (95% interval 1,912–4,607) and 4,663 t O2 (4,016–5,563).

At the smallest assumed 0.35 km3 receiving volume, point-estimate demand-to-standing-oxygen ratios were 1.20 and 1.58, but the paper explicitly says these are relative-magnitude screening metrics, not hypoxia probabilities or reconstructions of realized oxygen depletion.
uncertainty_and_limitations: Single altered estuary with a major reclamation intervention unlike ordinary Mobile Bay conditions.
Retrospective reconstruction combines observations from different years and assumptions about complete decomposition, affected fractions and receiving-water volume.
No direct reconstruction of realized oxygen depletion, no fish endpoint and no forecast validation.
Bootstrap intervals are conditional on the model and inputs; they do not cover all structural uncertainty.
mobile_bay_implications: Suggests benthic biological/organic-matter legacy can create a multi-week oxygen-demand memory after abrupt circulation or habitat changes.
Supports offline examination of sediment oxygen demand and recent-event persistence only if Mobile Bay-specific benthic and oxygen data exist.
Does not justify a new production feature, weight or physical collection program.
research_questions: Is there evidence of persistent benthic oxygen demand after major runoff, resuspension or habitat-disturbance episodes in Mobile Bay?
Can oxygen-loading memory be estimated from existing benthic/organic-matter observations without introducing unverified proxies?
Would a state-space oxygen-load term improve held-out event calibration once direct bottom oxygen and controls exist?

excluded_candidates.title: Spatiotemporal extent of diel and episodic hypoxia in bottom water of a shallow, well-mixed estuary
excluded_candidates.reason: Paper was published 2026-08-31, before the initial 2026-10-07 coverage window. An October institutional/news release did not create a new version or new empirical result.

excluded_candidates.title: Variation in hypoxia tolerance is driven by evolutionary adaptation in the eastern oyster
excluded_candidates.reason: New preprint and biologically relevant, but lower direct relevance to dissolved-oxygen/event forecasting than the three included papers; monitor for peer-reviewed version and forecasting implications.

excluded_candidates.title: Remote sensing of aquatic nutrients from proxy estimation to integration with process models
excluded_candidates.reason: Review/synthesis without new directly applicable estuarine oxygen-event validation; excluded under no-padding rule.

synthesis.strongest_new_evidence: Storm-driven dissolved-oxygen response is system- and salinity-dependent; the Weeks Bay-inclusive study argues against a simple universal rainfall sign.
synthesis.most_practical_methodological_update: High-frequency, depth-explicit, co-timed oxygen/salinity/temperature/met/current measurements with automated QC are a prerequisite for process attribution, but Tampa's near-surface network is not a substitute for Eastern Shore bottom oxygen.
synthesis.hypothesis_update: Retain rainfall/runoff interactions and benthic oxygen-load memory as research hypotheses only. Neither has met the production promotion gate.

offline_validation_opportunities: Construct leakage-safe storm-event windows for existing Weeks Bay and Eastern Shore observations and test sign heterogeneity by salinity/mixing state.
Audit existing source timestamps/depth/QC to determine whether 15-minute aligned oxygen-current-met windows are feasible without new collection.
Test a sediment/oxygen-load memory term only after direct bottom oxygen and matched event/control labels become sufficient.

guardrails: Peer review alone is not independent validation.
A successful oxygen or monitoring workflow is not Jubilee-event accuracy.
No feature receives positive production weight from plausibility or a single study.
No production probability, threshold, camera coverage, cadence, schedule, UNKNOWN rule or 9 p.m. gate changed.
No paid call, purchase, service activation, outreach, LinkedIn action or budget/billing change occurred.
